nodes.name: Cluster Operator
nodes.description: Administrator who provisions the Kairos host, installs k0s, deploys the sceau systemd unit, and points the k0s apiserver EncryptionConfiguration at the sceau unix socket.

nodes.name: Kairos OS Host (k0s control plane)
nodes.description: A single Kairos OS machine running the k0s control plane. The kube-apiserver, sceau, etcd, and the TPM all live on this host — there is no network hop between any of them.

nodes.name: kube-apiserver (k0s)
nodes.description: Kubernetes API server run by k0s as a host process. Generates a DEK per encrypted write and delegates envelope encryption to the KMS v2 plugin; persists the resulting envelopes in etcd.

nodes.name: sceau (KMS v2 plugin)
nodes.description: Rust gRPC daemon implementing the Kubernetes KMS v2 KeyManagementService (Status/Encrypt/Decrypt). Seals DEKs under a deterministic TPM SRK primary and unseals them on demand. Stateless: the SRK is recreated from its template at every startup.

nodes.name: etcd (k0s)
nodes.description: Cluster state store. Holds only KMS envelopes: the wrapped DEKs (TPM-sealed blobs) and the AES-GCM-encrypted Secret payloads. No plaintext key material is ever persisted.

nodes.name: TPM 2.0
nodes.description: Hardware root of trust on the Kairos host, reached through the in-kernel resource manager (/dev/tpmrm0). Hosts the deterministic RSA-2048 SRK primary; sealed DEK objects are fixedTpm+fixedParent and cannot leave the chip.

nodes.name: Sealed DEK envelope
nodes.description: The ciphertext sceau returns to the apiserver: version byte || marshaled TPM public area || TPM private blob of a sealed keyed-hash object. Useless without the originating TPM.

nodes.name: EncryptionConfiguration
nodes.description: k0s apiserver configuration (EncryptionConfiguration + extraArgs) that registers sceau as the v2 KMS provider for secrets, with the unix socket endpoint.

relationships.description: Every runtime component — the k0s apiserver, the sceau plugin, etcd, and the TPM — lives on the same Kairos host. The security boundary is the host itself.
The apiserver calls sceau's KMS v2 gRPC service (Status/Encrypt/Decrypt) over a host unix socket created with mode 0600, so only root — and thus the apiserver — can reach it.

sceau talks to the TPM through the TCTI (default device:/dev/tpmrm0): TPM2_CreatePrimary to recreate the deterministic SRK at startup, TPM2_Create to seal each DEK, TPM2_Load + TPM2_Unseal to decrypt.
The apiserver persists Secrets in etcd as KMS envelopes: sealed DEK plus AES-GCM ciphertext. etcd never sees plaintext DEKs or Secret payloads.
Sealed DEK envelopes are stored in etcd as part of the KMS v2 envelope format alongside each encrypted object.
The cluster operator deploys sceau (systemd unit) and writes the EncryptionConfiguration that points the apiserver at the sceau socket.

flows.name: sceau startup: recreate the SRK
flows.description: At boot (before the apiserver starts) sceau connects to the TPM and recreates the deterministic SRK primary from the standard template — identical key material on every boot of the same TPM — then derives the stable key_id from the SRK Name.

transitions.description: TPM2_CreatePrimary(Owner, SRK template) recreates the same RSA-2048 restricted decryption primary; the SRK handle is kept resident for the daemon's lifetime.
TPM2_ReadPublic yields the SRK Name; its hash becomes the KMS key_id reported by Status, stable across reboots of this TPM.

flows.name: Encrypt a Secret write
flows.description: The apiserver generates a DEK for a write, sceau seals it under the SRK, and the envelope is persisted in etcd.

transitions.description: Encrypt RPC: the apiserver sends the freshly generated DEK over the unix socket.
TPM2_Create builds a fixedTpm+fixedParent sealed keyed-hash object under the SRK containing the DEK; the private+public blobs never expose the DEK.
sceau returns the sealed envelope (version || public || private) as the KMS ciphertext with the current key_id.
The apiserver wraps the Secret payload with the DEK (AES-GCM) and stores the KMS envelope in etcd.

flows.name: Decrypt a Secret read
flows.description: On a read, the apiserver hands the stored envelope back to sceau, which unseals the DEK inside the TPM; plaintext crosses only the host-local socket.

transitions.description: The apiserver reads the KMS envelope (sealed DEK + ciphertext) for the requested object.
Decrypt RPC: the envelope is sent to sceau with its key_id; a mismatched key_id is rejected without touching the TPM.
TPM2_Load + TPM2_Unseal recover the DEK inside the TPM; the object handle is flushed immediately after.
The DEK returns over the unix socket and lives only in apiserver memory for the duration of the request.

tpm-root-of-trust.description: All DEK confidentiality is anchored in the TPM: the SRK primary is recreated from a deterministic template (never stored), and every sealed object is fixedTpm+fixedParent so it cannot be duplicated off the chip. TPM loss therefore means data loss — an accepted, documented trade-off.

no-persistent-plaintext.description: No plaintext key material is ever persisted: DEKs exist only in apiserver/plugin memory and inside the TPM; etcd holds only sealed envelopes; the KMS socket is mode 0600 on the host.

config.evidence: src/main.rs (socket mode 0600), src/kms.rs (no disk writes), docs/adr/0001-tpm-sealed-kms-v2-plugin.md

supply-chain-pipeline.description: Released artifacts carry supply-chain evidence: CycloneDX SBOM for the binary, a distroless digest-pinned container image Cosign-signed (keyless) by digest, and Trivy scanning with SARIF upload. All third-party actions are SHA-pinned; the workflow token is read-only by default with job-level elevation.
